ai.title: CLI exits with message when started in home directory
ai.summary: Codebuff CLI now displays a welcome message and calls `process.exit()` if `getProjectRoot()` equals `os.homedir()`. Previously, it printed startup instructions and returned, allowing the process to continue running without a valid project context. This change enforces that the agent must be run from within a specific project directory. The exit logic was moved from `displayGreeting` in `menu.ts` to the shutdown handler in `cli.ts` to ensure clean termination.

eli5.text: If you try to start the coding assistant while sitting in your home folder, it now prints a short welcome message and stops right away instead of staying open and showing instructions. You'll see steps telling you to change into a project folder and run the assistant again, and the program exits cleanly rather than continuing to run. This means the assistant must always be launched from inside a specific project directory.

ai.title: Fix carriage return logic in display.ts
ai.summary: Updated addCarriageReturn in npm-app/src/display.ts to handle newline conversion more robustly. Replaced manual double-replacement logic with a lookbehind regex (?<!\r)\n to ensure \r is only added when missing. Fixed previous state handling to prevent copying stray \n characters from the previous buffer.

eli5.text: When text appears on your screen, the software now handles line breaks more carefully, so characters display in the right spot without extra symbols or shifting. This behind-the-scenes tweak affects how the display looks moment to moment, and you'd notice smoother, cleaner line transitions if you were watching closely.

ai.title: Fix terminal hang on Windows echo line processing
ai.summary:
Replaced bulk `replaceAll` with looped `replace` in `runCommandPty` to prevent premature clearing of echo lines. Added `
` to `cd` command write in assistant mode to ensure proper execution. Scope limited to `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`. Fixes Windows terminal hangs caused by incorrect echo line counting and missing newline in directory change commands.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the terminal, the assistant now waits for the correct number of echo lines to finish before proceeding, fixing a bug where the terminal would freeze on Windows. Additionally, when the assistant changes directories, it now includes a newline character to ensure the command executes properly. These changes mean you'll no longer experience the terminal hanging when running commands in assistant mode on Windows.

ai.title: Clarify working directory in prompts and tool docs
ai.summary: Updated main-prompt.ts and tools.ts to explicitly handle current working directory (cwd) distinctions. Non-GeminiPro models now receive a system instruction that tool calls run from project root unless specified, while GeminiPro retains specific toolsInstructions. The user/assistant cwd context message format was standardized across prompt sections to clearly separate 'Assistant cwd (project root)' from 'User cwd'. Tools documentation now includes a dedicated Working Directory section emphasizing the need to resolve user-relative paths against the project root.

eli5.text: The software now more clearly explains where file work happens. When the assistant looks for or saves files, it works from your project's main folder unless you say otherwise, and new guidance reminds it to treat your current folder and the project folder as separate things. If you watched the assistant in action, you’d see it follow paths written from the project root rather than your open folder. This took effect on 2025-05-20 as part of a minor update.

ai.title: main-prompt injects explicit assistant cwd
ai.summary: backend/src/main-prompt.ts now injects agentState.fileContext.currentWorkingDirectory directly into the system message, replacing the vague 'assistant cwd is project root' text. This ensures the model receives the precise working directory path for accurate file operations. Scope limited to backend prompt generation.

eli5.text: When the assistant figures out which folder it's working in, it now gets the exact path instead of a guessing-game placeholder. If you watched the background messages it uses to stay oriented, you would see two separate lines: one for your folder and one for the assistant's folder, instead of a single line that hand-waved the assistant's location. This affects every conversation that starts a new task, and it's live today.

ai.title: Add slash command completion to CLI
ai.summary: CLI input handling now supports slash-prefixed commands via `getSlashCommands` and `displaySlashCommandGrid`. The `inputCompleter` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` intercepts lines starting with `/` to provide tab-completion for defined commands, falling back to file path completion otherwise. `npm-app/src/menu.ts` exports the `CommandInfo` interface and `interactiveCommandDetails` array to drive this behavior.

eli5.text: Starting today, if you begin typing a slash followed by a letter in the command line, you'll see a list of available shortcuts (like /login or /diff) appear so you can finish the command with the tab key instead of typing it all out. The feature only activates when the line starts with /, and if nothing matches, it quietly falls back to the normal file-path suggestions. It's live now for anyone running the interactive command-line tool.

ai.title: CLI clears pastedContent on freshPrompt
ai.summary: Clears `this.pastedContent` in `freshPrompt` within `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Prevents stale clipboard data from persisting across prompt resets. Internal refactor.

eli5.text: When you paste text into a fresh prompt in the CLI tool, any previously pasted content is now cleared automatically, preventing stale clipboard data from persisting across prompt resets. This affects developers using the command-line interface who may have unintentionally reused old pasted text in new prompts. You would notice that pasted content no longer lingers after starting a new prompt, keeping your input history clean and preventing accidental reuse of outdated clipboard data. This refinement is part of ongoing internal maintenance to improve the reliability of prompt handling.

ai.title: Rename Diagnostics Check to Project Setup in CLI menu
ai.summary: Header label in npm-app/src/menu.ts changed from 'DIAGNOSTICS CHECK' to 'PROJECT SETUP'. Internal UI text adjustment. No functional logic changes.

eli5.text: The command-line assistant's opening menu now calls its first step "PROJECT SETUP" instead of "DIAGNOSTICS CHECK." If you start the tool from your terminal, the bold header you see at the top will read PROJECT SETUP, but everything else - the options, what happens when you pick one, and what each step actually does - stays exactly the same. This is purely a relabeling so the name matches what users said the step feels like it does: getting their project ready rather than just checking on it. The change is live today in the assistant's command-line menus.

ai.title: Wrap user prompt in tags
ai.summary: Added asUserMessage helper in backend/src/util/messages.ts to wrap strings in <user_message> tags. Applied to user role content in mainPrompt within backend/src/main-prompt.ts. Ensures clear distinction of user inputs from system instructions in the prompt structure.

eli5.text: When the assistant receives your message, it now wraps your input in clear labels that tell the system 'this is a user message' before passing it along with the instructions it follows. The effect is that the assistant can better tell apart what you wrote from the background directions it runs on, so your questions are less likely to get mixed up with its internal setup. If you watched closely, you'd see your prompt appears neatly bracketed instead of sitting directly beside the rules. This is live today and affects how your messages are processed behind the scenes.

ai.title: Add /init command alias to backend prompts
ai.summary: The `/init` string is added as a key in `additionalSystemPrompts` alongside `init`, both mapping to the same `initPrompt` constant. This ensures the initialization flow triggers correctly when users type `/init`. The change is internal to `backend/src/system-prompt/prompts.ts`.

eli5.text: Typing either '/init' or just 'init' in the assistant now starts the same setup process, so you no longer need to use a specific phrasing to kick off initialization. Internally, the system now recognizes both of these as equivalent triggers for the same initialization workflow. If you looked, you'd see the assistant respond the same way regardless of which command form you used. This change is live today.

ai.title: Simplify interactive command menu display
ai.summary: Removes redundant 'type ' prefixes from commandText strings in npm-app/src/menu.ts. Updates section header to 'COMMANDS (type these below)' and consolidates footer prompts into a single line. Internal UI polish for CLI help menu.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant's help menu, the list of commands no longer shows the word 'type' before each command name, and the header now reads 'COMMANDS (type these below)' to make it clearer that you literally type those commands. The two separate lines telling you what to do next have been merged into a single line that says 'Thanks for using Codebuff! Enter a prompt below ↓'. If you looked at the menu now, the command list would look less cluttered and a bit easier to scan.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to update itself and something goes wrong, it now quietly records the specific error message before showing the usual 'Failed to update' message. The program now keeps track of what went wrong, even if you never see it, so the team can find out when updates are breaking and why. This only affects the part of the program that handles updating the assistant itself, nothing else.

ai.summary: Prepends 'Thanks for using Codebuff!' to the community feedback line. Replaces the closing prompt with '↓ Enter your prompt or command below ↓'. Affects only the CLI help menu output.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant's help menu, the text that thanked you for using Codebuff now appears first, right before contact information. The final line, which you saw after reviewing all the menu options, changed from 'Thanks for using Codebuff! Enter a prompt below ↓' to '↓ Enter your prompt or command below ↓'. You won't notice any difference in how the assistant works, just how these two lines read.

ai.title: Fix help command table spacing
ai.summary: Adjusts header spacing in the CLI help command table by reducing the fixed width padding calculation. The change corrects alignment between the COMMANDS and DESCRIPTION headers in npm-app/src/menu.ts. This is a cosmetic fix for the menu rendering logic.

eli5.text: When you open the help menu in the command-line tool, the column headers for "COMMANDS" and "DESCRIPTION" now line up correctly, instead of the spacing looking slightly off. This cosmetic adjustment affects anyone who uses the text-based menu by typing the help command, and you'd notice the two headers appearing more neatly aligned across from each other.

ai.title: Fix Ctrl/Cmd click hint in menu
ai.summary: Updated the Discord join prompt in `npm-app/src/menu.ts` to dynamically display 'Command' or 'Ctrl' based on `os.platform()`. Replaced the static '(Ctrl/Cmd+Click to open)' string with a conditional template literal and changed the text color from `yellow` to `gray`.

eli5.text: When you start the tool and it shows the link to join its Discord chat, the hint that tells you how to click the link now matches your computer's operating system. On Windows and Linux it reads 'Ctrl + Click to open,' while on a Mac it reads 'Command + Click to open,' instead of always showing the generic 'Ctrl/Cmd' wording. The hint text also changed from yellow to gray so it sits more quietly next to the link. This is a small, behind-the-scenes tweak to the startup menu, and it's live today.

ai.title: Quit in root directory
ai.summary: Added root directory check to the project root validation in `npm-app/src/menu.ts`. The agent now quits if `getProjectRoot()` returns `/` or the user's home directory. This prevents execution in unsafe contexts.

eli5.text: The coding assistant now also refuses to start if you try to run it from the very top of your computer's file system (the root directory), in addition to the home directory it already blocked. If you were to launch it there, it simply quits instead of running. This keeps it from operating in places where it shouldn't, protecting against accidental use in overly broad locations.

ai.summary: Added 'run init to fix' hints for missing knowledge.md and codebuff.json. Updated conditional rendering in npm-app/src/menu.ts. Internal repo change.

eli5.text: When the menu checks your project setup and finds that key files like knowledge.md or codebuff.json are missing, it now tells you exactly what to do about it by showing a hint that says to run 'init' to fix the issue. Previously, the menu would just report that those files were missing without guiding you on how to resolve it. You would notice this next time you open the menu and see warnings about missing files accompanied by clear instructions to run 'init', making it easier to set up your project correctly.

ai.title: Restore classic randomized coloring in menu
ai.summary: Reverts random character coloring in `displayMenu` to pick 3 distinct colors from a pool of 7 (`red`, `green`, `yellow`, `blue`, `blueBright`, `magenta`, `cyan`) before rendering, rather than choosing from a fixed 5-color list per character. Updates `npm-app/src/menu.ts` to import `blue`, `red`, and `Formatter` from `picocolors`. The new `getRandomColors` helper ensures consistent palette selection per menu invocation.

eli5.text: When you open the interactive menu in the assistant's command-line tool, the characters of the welcome text now get colored using a fresh random mix of three distinct colors pulled from a set of seven options, rather than the previous fixed set of five colors. The selection of those three colors is made once per menu display, so every character on a given screen uses one of the same three colors instead of a completely independent choice for each one. This only affects people running the assistant from the terminal, and it is a purely cosmetic change: you will notice the welcome banner looking slightly different each time you open it, with a guaranteed minimum of three different colors but no new functionality attached.

ai.title: readfiles prompt update
ai.summary: Prompt for `read_files` tool in `backend/src/tools.ts` updated. New instruction explicitly forbids re-reading files already in context, noting changes surface via file update results. Internal change to backend tool definitions.

eli5.text: The assistant will no longer try to read a file it has already read during the same session, because seeing the file once gives it everything it needs. Any future edits to that file appear to it automatically as they happen, so re-reading would just waste time. This is purely an internal tweak to how the assistant is instructed to work, and you would not notice anything different in your interactions today.

ai.title: SIGINT double-press exit skips active input
ai.summary: CLI SIGINT handler now checks `this.rl.line` before triggering exit on double-press. Prevents accidental termination when user has recently typed. Logic in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: When you're typing a question and press Ctrl+C twice quickly to quit the assistant, it now waits to make sure you really meant to quit, if you've just typed something, it won't close. This only affects the small group of people running the tool directly in their terminal, and it's active today.

ai.title: Add prompting for background process management
ai.summary: Updated system prompts in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/system-prompt/prompts.ts` to enforce proper background process handling. Instructions now mandate killing entire process groups (or trees on Windows) using SIGTERM signals and restarting processes with `process_type=BACKGROUND`. This change aims to prevent orphaned processes and ensure cleaner lifecycle management for background tasks.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts a background task, it now knows to shut it down properly by stopping the whole group of related processes at once (using the gentler SIGTERM signal) instead of leaving zombie processes behind, and when it restarts a task it makes sure that task knows to run in the background so it doesn't accidentally block or freeze your terminal. If you ever watched the assistant forget to clean up a long-running process or leave your command line stuck, you would see fewer of those problems now because the assistant was given clearer instructions on how to handle those background jobs safely.

ai.title: Switch saxy stream import to node:stream
ai.summary: common/src/util/saxy.ts replaces readable-stream with node:stream for the Transform import. Removes external polyfill dependency in favor of native Node APIs. Scope limited to shared core utility module. No migration or behavior change required.

eli5.text: The assistant's underlying data-processing engine now uses a built-in part of the system software instead of a separate add-on tool it was borrowing. This swap only affects an internal piece of shared code used to handle streaming data, so most people won't notice anything different. It's a small housekeeping change that quietly removes an outdated extra tool the system was relying on.

Menu display function renamed to displaySlashCommandHelperMenu with improved formatting including command descriptions and shell tip. Login command marked as non-slash command in interactiveCommandDetails. Slash command list now sorted alphabetically.

eli5.text: When you type a slash command at the prompt, the assistant now shows a sorted, better-formatted menu with descriptions and a shell tip, and it tells you clearly if you mistype a command. Referral-style commands still accept the slash, but it is stripped before processing. The change is live today for anyone using the interactive command prompt where they type commands directly.

ai.title: Fix unit tests in main-prompt
ai.summary: Corrects assertions in `main-prompt` integration and unit tests. Updates import order and fixes newline escaping in `getMessageText`. Aligns expected user prompt content with `asUserMessage` helper output.

eli5.text: The app's internal checks that make sure its main instructions work correctly had some mistakes in their expected results, so those test expectations were corrected. This only affects the development team's behind-the-scenes quality checks; regular users wouldn't notice any change in how the app behaves.

ai.title: System prompt tweaks and XML parser error message update
ai.summary: Updated `main-prompt.ts` to instruct the agent to correct system errors alongside assistant mistakes. Refined `agent-instructions.md` wording for clarity on end-turn behavior. Modified `xml-stream-parser.ts` to change the warning message for stray XML tags from 'Ignoring stray XML tag' to 'Tool not found', including an HTML-escaped example in the error output.

eli5.text: When the assistant sees something went wrong in a previous attempt (including errors from the system itself, not just mistakes by the assistant), it now tries to fix those errors along with any other mistakes. The error message shown for unrecognized commands was updated to be clearer, now saying "Tool not found" and including an example of how to properly format text so it isn't mistaken for a command.

ai.title: Add analytics for slash command usage
ai.summary: Added `SLASH_MENU_ACTIVATED`, `SLASH_COMMAND_USED`, and `INVALID_COMMAND` events to `AnalyticsEvent` enum in `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`. `npm-app/src/cli.ts` now tracks these events via `trackEvent` when users activate the slash menu, execute valid commands, or enter unknown slash commands. Includes user ID and command string in payload for successful and invalid commands. Menu activation tracking is gated to ensure it only fires when '/' is the sole character in the input line.

eli5.text: When you type a slash command in the assistant, the system now quietly records that you used it, whether you picked a real command or typed something unrecognized. You won't see anything new on screen, but the team can now see how often the slash menu is opened, which commands are used, and which mistakes people make. This only happens after today's update, and it applies to everyone using the assistant.

ai.title: npm-app version bump to 1.0.286
ai.summary: Version in npm-app/package.json bumped 1.0.285 to 1.0.286. Internal release increment. No feature or behavior changes.

eli5.text: The Codebuff assistant's app version was bumped from 1.0.285 to 1.0.286, a routine update that keeps the installed version current. This release bundles the latest changes the Codebuff team built, like a clearer welcome message when you're in the wrong folder, smoother typing that no longer freezes on Windows, and a new quick-command menu you can open by typing slashes (e.g., /init). Updating to this version is what delivers those improvements to you.

ai.title: Fix xml-stream-parser test expectation
ai.summary: Updated `xml-stream-parser.test.ts` to expect the new warning message 'WARN: Tool not found. Make sure to escape non-tool XML! e.g. <invalid>'. This aligns the test with the current error handling logic for stray XML tags.

eli5.text: The assistant will now show a clearer warning message when it encounters XML tags that are not valid tool calls, such as a missing or misspelled tool tag. Instead of the previous generic warning about stray XML, the message now explains that the tool was not found and provides an example of how to properly escape non-tool XML content. This change only updates the expected message used in automated tests to match the current behavior, and it is already in place today.

ai.title: Context7 API v1 migration and query-based search
ai.summary: Backend Context7 integration migrated to `https://context7.com/api/v1/search` for dynamic library lookup, replacing static project listing. `get-documentation-for-query.ts` now performs a two-step flow: AI-driven library suggestion followed by parallel documentation fetching. `context7-api.ts` exports `searchLibraries` and updates `fetchContext7LibraryDocumentation` to accept queries instead of pre-resolved IDs. This removes the `context7LibrariesPromise` singleton in favor of on-demand search.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant for documentation about a programming library, it now searches for the right library in real time using a newer search API, instead of picking from a fixed pre-loaded list. This means the assistant can find and fetch documentation for libraries it wasn't previously programmed to know about, as long as you describe what you're looking for in your question. The behind-the-scenes lookup is live today, so you may get results from libraries that were previously unavailable.

ai.title: Increase timeout for context 7
ai.summary: Adjusted timeout and chunk limits in `get-documentation-for-query.ts`. Increased Gemini response timeout from 12s to 20s and capped unique chunks at 25. Updated error logging to explicitly extract message and stack from Error objects. Enforced max 3 libraries/topics in prompt instructions.

eli5.text: The assistant now waits longer for its research tool to answer your question, so it is less likely to give up and return nothing when the tool takes a bit of time. It also limits the amount of source material it processes at once, which keeps responses from getting cut off, and records clearer error details if something still goes wrong. You would notice this if you asked a question that used to time out or fail silently: it should now return an answer where it previously returned nothing.

ai.title: Add file-picker grading infrastructure and relabel UI updates
ai.summary: Introduce grade-run subsystem for evaluating file-selection model outputs via LLM judge, with new backend grading logic and BigQuery trace schema support. Add admin relabel runs UI page and expand trace retrieval to bundle related training-context traces. Update client.ts to support optional user filtering and INNER/LEFT join types for trace queries.

eli5.text: The tool that helps decide which code files matter most for a request can now be automatically graded by another AI model, so teams can see how well different versions perform side by side in a new admin page. When an admin opens that page, they will find a new section for relabeling past decisions, and the backend now pulls in extra context from related training traces to help make those judgments. Support staff and internal users will notice the new grading and relabeling pages are available today, while the underlying query system now also lets developers ask for traces with or without associated relabels or training-context data using optional filters.

ai.title: Admin relabel limit configurable and full context counter fix
ai.summary: Added a UI setting in web/src/app/admin/file-picker/page.tsx to configure the relabel limit, replacing the hardcoded value of 10. Fixed a logic error in backend/src/admin/relabelRuns.ts where the relabeled counter incremented per trace instead of per successful relabel action within the full context loop. The fix introduces a didRelabel flag to ensure accurate counting when multiple relabel types are triggered for a single trace. Scope limited to internal admin tools for relabel runs.

eli5.text: Admins who use the internal file picker can now choose how many runs get relabeled at once, instead of it being locked to 10. While that list is loading, the system counts each run that actually gets relabeled once and only once, even if two different labeling methods kick in for the same run. If you watched the counter tick up, you used to see it jump higher than the real number of relabeled runs; now it matches what really happened. This is live for internal admin tools today.
